{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"King's Highway 95, commonly referred to as Highway 95, was a provincially maintained highway in the Canadian province of Ontario on Wolfe Island.","title":"Ontario Highway 95"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Together with Highway 96, the highways were the only King's Highways not connected to the rest of the network by a fixed link.","title":"Ontario Highway 95"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" At its southern end, the route connected to New York State Route 12E via the private and seasonal Horne's Ferry.","title":"Ontario Highway 95"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" At its northern end, the route connected with Highway 96 in Marysville a short distance west of the Wolfe Islander III ferry to Kingston.","title":"Ontario Highway 95"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" Today, it is known as Frontenac County Road 95.","title":"Ontario Highway 95"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Highway 93 is a north–south route through the southeastern part of British Columbia, in the Regional District of East Kootenay and takes its number from U.S. Highway 93 that it connects with at the Canada-U.S. border.","title":"British Columbia Highway 93"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It follows the Crowsnest Highway (Highway 3) and Highway 95 through Radium Hot Springs and to where it crosses the Continental Divide into Alberta at Vermilion Pass, where it continues as Alberta Highway 93.","title":"British Columbia Highway 93"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The section between the Canada-U.S. border and the Crowsnest Highway is known as the Elko–Roosville Highway, the section between the Crowsnest Highway and Radium Hot Springs is known as the Kootenay–Columbia Highway, while the section east of Radium Hot Srings is known as the Banff–Windermere Parkway.","title":"British Columbia Highway 93"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"One of the only Interstate highways to cross from Mexico to Canada The highway connects with U.S. Highway 95 at the Canada-U.S. border at?"}
